author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: GH-1665: extension flag contracts omit the SDK option key, so PmClient.run and the extension test harness silently ignore a CLI-spelled option such as status-filter and fall back to the default

GitHub issue #1665 (reported 2026-11-04 against 2026.11.4, found while authoring an extension from the published docs). An extension command declares --status-filter, reads options.statusFilter and defaults to open. On the CLI, pm demo-brief --status-filter closed returns closed items. Through PmClient.run('demo-brief', { options }) and through the extension test harness, options { statusFilter: 'closed' } returns closed items, but options { 'status-filter': 'closed' } silently returns the default open selection, with no refusal or warning. pm contracts --command demo-brief --flags-only --json lists --status-filter and nothing names the handler key statusFilter, so a caller copying the contract's spelling cannot learn the right key. Source is consistent with the report: the definition-driven extension option normalizer lives in src/cli/extension-command-options.ts and is consumed only by the CLI host (src/cli/main.ts and src/cli/runtime/invocation-options.ts), not by the SDK run path. Fleet packages work around it: the pm-brief package reads both include-history and includeHistory and accepts string booleans from direct callers. Expected: runtime flag contracts expose the handler key for every extension flag (for example sdk_option), and at the SDK boundary a known CLI-spelled option is normalized exactly as the host parser does, or refused naming the canonical key, with conflicting aliases refused. Why it matters for agents: an agent builds valid-looking context from the wrong lifecycle bucket and nothing tells it that its selection input was ignored. Related: pm-7lv8yx owns the inverse spelling leak (typed SDK refusals that name CLI flags), pm-11phn1 (GH-817) defined the invocation metadata that command_flags exposes, which has no option key, and pm-ill9gv (GH-719) routed host-owned globals to context.global. Duplicate check: searched extension flag option key, PmClient.run extension options, kebab and camel option normalization and harness parsed options across all statuses, and no item owns the extension flag-to-handler key mapping.

Every extension flag row in pm contracts --command <cmd> --flags-only --json and in pm help <cmd> --json carries the handler option key the command receives (for example sdk_option: statusFilter), derived from the same declaration the host parser uses; PmClient.run and the extension test harness normalize a declared CLI spelling such as status-filter to the handler key exactly as CLI dispatch does, or refuse with a typed error naming the canonical key, through one definition-driven normalizer shared with CLI dispatch; Passing two spellings of one declared flag with different values is refused with a typed conflict error naming both keys; A spec drives one extension command through CLI argv, PmClient.run with each spelling, and the harness, asserting the same selection, and a negative control that removes the SDK-side normalization fails it; docs/SDK.md and docs/EXTENSIONS.md state which key a direct caller passes and show the contract field

Declare an extension command with --status-filter read as options.statusFilter (default open). pm demo-brief --status-filter closed returns closed. PmClient.run('demo-brief', { options: { 'status-filter': 'closed' } }) returns open with no warning
A CLI-spelled extension option passed to PmClient.run or the harness is normalized like CLI dispatch or refused naming the handler key, and contracts publish that key
options { 'status-filter': 'closed' } through PmClient.run or the harness silently returns the default open selection, and contracts list only --status-filter

message: Triage GitHub issue #1665 into the tracker
